analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. Both supplied units are BASE text of that file, and the HEAD patch excerpt is truncated. The changes visible in the patch are documentation only:
- A 15-second per-model unload bound at shutdown, citing ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown. A model whose native retirement never finishes is left to process exit.
- A rewrite of the status docs for the enabled_models restart-needed notice (enabled_models_at_start, enabled_models_at_last_switch), plus a 'Retrying <model> when memory frees' line.
No code, controls, endpoints or configuration changed.

Threat-model relevance: the 15 s bound on unload interacts with T-028 (residual GPU/KV data after shutdown), T-010 and A-018. A stuck model is left to process exit. That is plausible, since the process terminating releases GPU memory, but the underlying Swift change is not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should check that bounded unload does not leave decrypted KV data or prefix-cache staging reservations (T-041) live beyond process exit, and that provider shutdown does not skip KEK or key zeroization. The cache file at rest is AES-GCM encrypted anyway.

The status documentation exposes only model-ID filter diffs, which are already public via heartbeats. It adds no new secret exposure. No existing doc claims about logout, revocation (A-008, T-053), or add-on hold (TB-012) were altered in the visible ranges.

No security regression is identified from the documentation. Because the patch excerpt is truncated and the described runtime behavior (ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown) is unverified, a code-side reviewer should confirm the shutdown behavior. I do not raise this as a finding.
